build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

comments.text: The level's character set, 256 characters to $5FFF, shared by levels 3.1 and 3.2 (level 3.2's file loads at $8700 and leaves it in place). Characters below first_clear ($40) are walls and floors to Clyde. level_frame scrolls some of them a pixel at a time and swaps the torches' frames; see the comments at each.

Character $4F of the level's character set, and the characters after it. The label is the engine's: wipe_char_set, called by the attract sequence, redefines character $4F here for a screen wipe; no code of the level calls it.
Characters $57-$60 of world 3's character set ($5AB8-$5B07): the world's 96 tiles use all of these, $60 most often (5 places); all multicolour by char_colours.

Character $61, the first of four ($61-$64) along the top of the strip of small arches by the castle floor; level 3.2's map draws them in its last stretch (columns 149-168), level 3.1's not at all. level_frame's arches_row_a (s_AA73) scrolls a row of all four together a pixel right: rows 0-4 every fifth frame and rows 5-7 every third, while the landscape scrolls and the scroll position is $90 or more.
Character $62, the second of the arches' top strip.
Character $63, the third of the arches' top strip.
Character $64, the last of the arches' top strip; arches_row_a carries its last bit round to $61.

Character $65 from its second row: the first of the arches' second strip, $65, $66, $67 and $6C, which arches_row_b (s_AA84) scrolls a row at a time: rows 1-2 every other frame, rows 4-7 on two frames in three; rows 0 and 3 stay put.
Character $66 from its second row, in the arches' second strip.
Character $67 from its second row, in the arches' second strip, and the four characters after it.
Character $6C from its second row, the last of the arches' second strip; arches_row_b carries its last bit round to $65.

Characters $74-$77, a torch on the castle wall (level 3.1's map has five from column 152, level 3.2's 26): level_frame copies one of two 32-byte frames over them every third frame, torch_frame_a and torch_frame_b in turn, so the flames flicker. The characters after them follow.

Character $A6, the first of the arches' third strip ($A6, $A7, $DE and $F3): level_frame scrolls all eight rows of the four together a pixel right on three frames in four.
Character $A7, in the arches' third strip, and the characters after it.
Characters $AF-$DD of world 3's character set ($5D78-$5EEF): the world's 96 tiles use all of these, $DC most often (115 places); 45 multicolour by char_colours.
Character $DE, in the arches' third strip, and the character after it.

Character $E1, in the distant graves above the wall.
Character $E2, in the distant graves above the wall.

Character $E6, in the upper half of the graves seen through the gaps.

Character $EA, in the lower half of the graves seen through the gaps.

Sprite blocks $F0-$FF of world 3's sprites ($7C00-$7FFF): $F0-$F7 a star that bursts and fades, a death; $F8-$FF a ball that breaks into sparks, a death.

Cold and warm start vectors for the KERNAL's cartridge test, both $AF6A (memory_wipe), followed at $8004 by the signature CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30). Every level and chamber file carries them, so a reset while this level is in memory runs memory_wipe and erases the game.

The level's 96 tiles, 16 bytes each to $8608: tile N is at $8009 + 16 x N (the engine's tables tile_addr_lo/hi at $B000/$B060). Each is four rows of four character numbers, top row first; scroll_draw_column draws a tile a column at a time, bytes c, c+4, c+8 and c+12 from the top, with each character's colour from char_colours. The map uses 81 of the 96 tiles.
Tile 4 from its ninth byte, and tiles 5-15. The label is the engine's: once a torture chamber's file is in, the engine's $BE5C jumps to $8051, where every chamber starts its code.
Tiles 8 to 15 ($08-$0F), from tile 8's ninth byte, 16 bytes each: the map draws all eight, tile $0B most often (262 times). j_8051, the label before, is the engine's, so its span ends 64 bytes on.
Tiles 16-31 ($10-$1F), 16 bytes each: the map draws 14 of them, tile $11 most often (41 times).
Tiles 32-47 ($20-$2F), 16 bytes each: the map draws 14 of them, tile $22 most often (10 times).
Tiles 48-63 ($30-$3F), 16 bytes each: the map draws 16 of them, tile $3C most often (32 times).
Tiles 64-79 ($40-$4F), 16 bytes each: the map draws 15 of them, tile $42 most often (13 times).
Tiles 80-95 ($50-$5F), 16 bytes each: the map draws 6 of them, tile $5A most often (5 times).

Tile 83 from its thirteenth byte, and the tiles after it to $8608. The label is the engine's: the raster routine's operand ($1106) still held $8545, torture chamber 2's raster_ledge_colour, at the hand-over.

The colour of each of the 256 characters, which scroll_draw_column writes to colour RAM with the character (bit 3 set makes the character multicolour; the low three bits are its colour): 215 of them are multicolour. The label is the engine's.
The addresses of the six map rows, two bytes each: $8715, $87D5, $8895, $8955, $8A15, $8AD5. scroll_column reads them for each new column. The label is the engine's.
map_row_addrs from its second byte: the high byte of row 0's address, and the other rows' (scroll_column reads the high bytes from $870A). The label is the engine's.

Map row 0, the top tile row: one tile number for each map column, 173 columns used of the 192 bytes (the level's length, $AD, at level_end). The row doubles as the column command table: a byte with bit 7 set makes its whole column a command that scroll_column carries out and skips, bit 6 set for the next six sky colours (level_colours_next), clear for the next four band routines (level_band_routines). Command columns: 0 (band routines), 1 (sky colours), 26 (band routines), 45 (sky colours), 74 (sky colours), 96 (sky colours), 147 (sky colours), 166 (band routines). The label is the engine's.

Map row 1 of six, the second tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 173 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0B. The label is the engine's.

Map row 2 of six, the third tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 173 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0B. The label is the engine's.

Map row 3 of six, the fourth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 173 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0B. The label is the engine's.

Map row 4 of six, the fifth tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 173 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0B. The label is the engine's.

Map row 5 of six, the bottom tile row (four character rows each): a tile number for each map column, 173 of its 192 bytes drawn; the bytes in command columns are skipped. Its commonest tile is $0B. The label is the engine's.

The level's length in map columns, $AD (173): scroll_column stops scrolling there ($1216) and wakes objects waiting for the end, and game_frame_music starts the end tune and object_kill counts the end creature's death within three columns of it. The label is the engine's.
The first character Clyde and his shots pass through, $40: player_control, its jump and fall, and shot_hits_wall treat every character below it as wall or floor.

Band colours for $D022, the characters' first multicolour (through $12BD-$12C2): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (the other never read): change 0: light green light green light red light green light red light red; change 1: grey grey grey light green light red light green; change 2: green green grey light green light green light green; change 3: green green green grey light green yellow; change 4: grey grey grey grey grey yellow. The label is the engine's.

Band colours for $D023, the second multicolour (through $12C3-$12C8): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (the other never read): change 0: grey grey orange orange orange orange; change 1: orange orange orange orange orange orange; change 2: orange orange orange orange orange orange; change 3: orange orange orange orange orange orange; change 4: orange orange orange orange orange orange. Band colours for $D021, the background (through $12C9-$12CE): six raster bands for each of six changes, which level_colours_next copies six at a time; the raster routines write a band's value at its top unless bit 7 is set, which leaves the colour from the band above. This level reads changes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (the other never read): change 0: dark grey dark grey dark grey brown brown brown; change 1: dark grey dark grey dark grey brown brown brown; change 2: dark grey dark grey dark grey brown brown brown; change 3: dark grey dark grey dark grey brown brown brown; change 4: dark grey dark grey dark grey dark grey dark grey brown. The label is the engine's.

The band table: four entries per change of band routines, for bands 2-5, each an index into the engine's routine table at $12CF (level_band_routines). This level reads groups 0, 1, 2 (the others never read): 0: 0 1 0 2; 1: 1 0 2 0; 2: 0 1 0 2. The label is the engine's.

print_big's string 1, the stage's name on the Get Ready screen: "STAGE 3.1" and $FF. The label is the engine's.
print_at's string 0, the Get Ready screen's first line, centred in 40 characters: "GRUESOME GRAVEYARD FOLLOWED BY" and $FF. The label is the engine's.

The colours of the Get Ready screen's three potion-creature icons, four sets of three: raster_ready_icons shows the last set first, then steps through the first three every ten frames. green white light blue; green light red white; white light red light blue; green light red light blue. The label is the engine's.
The stage's time limit, three digits: 500. timer_reset copies them to the panel's timer. The label is the engine's.

The level's five hook addresses, copied by level_begin into the engine's calls: $A95F every frame (level_frame_call), $A39A for Clyde (level_player_call), $A3C5 for his jump (level_jump_call), $A50D for his animation (level_anim_call) and $A537 in place of firing (level_hook_call). The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' second address, the player routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' third address, the jump routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fourth address, the animation routine. The label is the engine's.
level_hooks' fifth address, called instead of player_fire. The label is the engine's.
The Get Ready strip's colours, read by raster_ready_strip: orange, dark grey (the two multicolour registers) and, at $8CF4, black for the background. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' second byte. The label is the engine's.
strip_colours' third byte, the strip's background. The label is the engine's.

end_tune_addr's high byte. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 56 object types' animation scripts; object_set_type and object_spawn read them with anim_hi. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the object types' animation scripts. The label is the engine's.
Each object type's animation speed: a new byte of its script every speed + 1 of the object's turns (each object animates every other frame); $7F all but stops it. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 15 colour cycles' lists, chosen by a spawn record's colour byte ($10-$1E) or a death's colour cycle. The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the colour cycles' lists. The label is the engine's.
Each colour cycle's speed: frames between its colours (obj_cycle_speed). The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 x movement scripts, named by a spawn record (byte 1, and byte 0's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the x movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
The low bytes of the 32 y movement scripts (record byte 2, and byte 10's high nibble at death). The label is the engine's.
The high bytes of the y movement scripts. The label is the engine's.
Hit points by the low nibble of record byte 9: $FF $00 $03 $06 $09 $0C $10 $18 $20 $30 $50 $80 $B0 $F8 $00 $FE ($FF: shots never harm it, they only make it flash). The label is the engine's.

Start delays, in frames, by the top two bits of record bytes 1 and 2 together: $00 $01 $02 $03 $04 $05 $10 $20 $30 $40 $50 $60 $06 $80 $FE $FF. The label is the engine's.
Hits needed before an object's hit response runs, by the low nibble of record byte 15: $00 $03 $06 $09 $10 $09 $0F $10 $20 $40 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $FF. The label is the engine's.

Clyde has touched the broomstick (frame $8F): player_hit jumps here (from $3CDA). Nothing happens if he already rides. Otherwise his hits left ($12A0) go to saved_hits and are zeroed, so anything that touches him on the broom kills him outright; the special state $122B is set (the level's routines take over his movement, frames and fire) with $1242 (no shots), $1213 (the panel shows its lower sprites) and $122A; his flame ends; the broomstick (object X from $3A) is removed; the x high bits of his other sprites are cleared ($1259, $125B); only Clyde's own sprite stays multicolour ($1286 = 1) and sprite 1 is doubled in width ($C056 = 2); the handle is brown ($1295 = 9) and the bristles light grey ($1297 = $0F, left in A by flame_end); panel sprite 1 shows pointer 6, the BROOM label (seen in play); and the gauge is filled (broom_refill) with its first step 51 frames away ($32). Then it falls into broom_place.

0, then broom_speeds: the climb and dive read their step from here by their speed (0 none), one place earlier than the sideways flight does.

The pixels the broom moves in a frame at each speed, 0-14: 1 0 1 1 0 1 1 1 2 1 2 2 1 2 2. Speed rises by one a frame while the joystick is held, to 13 sideways and 14 up or down, so the broom gathers pace over a quarter of a second, and settles at 2 pixels a frame.

Clyde's routine for this level (level_hooks' second, run by player_control each frame). On the broom it goes back into player_control at $2C63, past the clearing of the special state. On foot it reads the character at offset $52 from his cell, two rows down and two across: $5F or $F2, the spikes of level 3.2's castle, clear his hits left ($12A0) and jump into player_hurt past its invulnerability test ($3CEC), so the spikes kill him whatever hits he had. The loop around the test (DEY, then CPY #$78 with BCS) never runs a second time, as Y is then $51. Otherwise it returns to player_control at $2C34.

The broom's flight (level_hooks' third, run instead of the engine's jump and fall while $122B is set). First the climb or dive (broom_climb). Then sideways: right held picks right, left held left, and with neither the speed of the way he flies ($1272: 0 left, 1 right) drops by one a frame until he stops. Pushing against the way he flies first brakes, a speed step a frame, and only then turns him; pushing with it raises the speed ($1268 for left, $1269 for right) to 13. The step comes from broom_speeds.
Flying left: $1272 = 0 and the left speed rises, to 13 at most.

Operand of the CMP at $A3FC ($1272), where right held compares the way he flies with right. The label is the engine's: level_hook_call's operand ($1BA6) still held $A3FD, world 2's level_fire, at the hand-over.
Flying right: $1272 = 1 and the right speed rises, to 13 at most.
Neither way held: the speed of the way he flies drops by one; at 0 he stops.

The move. Flying left, the three characters in the column of his cell (offsets 0, $28 and $50) must all be first_clear or above, or he stays; the step goes into the engine's left step ($2CD6). Flying right, with $88/$89 set a row above his cell, it tests the column three to the right (offsets 3, $2B and $53) and passes the step to player_set_speed, which also sets the scroll's speed.
LDA #0 and STA into $1272, $1268 and $1269, then RTS: twelve bytes that would stop the broom dead, which no JSR, JMP or branch reaches.

The broom's up and down, from level_jump: up or down held ($127C, $127D) sets the direction ($126B: 0 up, 1 down) and raises the speed $126A by one a frame, to 14; with neither held the speed drops by one a frame, and at 0 both are cleared. Pressing the other way turns him at once, at the speed he had.
The climb or dive at the speed in $126A.

Diving: the speed goes into the LDX's operand at $A4DA; he stops if any of the three characters three rows below his cell (offsets $78-$7A) is below first_clear, and otherwise his y ($1282) grows by broom_steps' entry for the speed.
Operand of the LDX at $A4DA: the dive's speed, written at $A4C8.

Climbing: the speed goes into the LDX's operand at $A500. Below y $3C, or with a character below first_clear at offset 1 or 2 from his cell, the climb stops and the speed is cleared; otherwise his y shrinks by broom_steps' entry for the speed.
Operand of the LDX at $A500: the climb's speed, written at $A4E7.

Clyde's frames while he rides (level_hooks' fourth). Every sixth frame ($122F from 5) the step $1244 moves on, 3 down to 0, though no frame here depends on it. The handle (shot sprite 1) takes broom_handle_frames and the bristles (shot sprite 2) broom_bristle_frames for the way he faces, and Clyde broom_rider_frames, stored by the engine at $2F07 ($1287), which then leaves the shots alone ($1242 is set).

Run in place of player_fire every frame Clyde rides (level_hooks' fifth), so the fire button does nothing on the broom: it drains the gauge (broom_drain) and puts the broom's sprites by him (broom_place).
The frames to the gauge's next step, counted down by broom_drain each frame and reloaded with $3E, so a step every 63 frames; broom_mount sets $32 for the first.
The gauge's byte columns left, 6 when full (broom_refill): broom_drain counts it down as each column empties, and a step with none left ends the ride.

The low bytes of the gauge's six byte columns, left to right: $40A7, $40A8, $40A9 in panel sprite block 2 and $40E7, $40E8, $40E9 in block 3, rows 13-20, under the score's digits. broom_drain empties them from the right.

AND masks that clear one two-bit pixel of a byte: broom_drain uses the first four, $3F $CF $F3 $FC, last to first, so a column empties from its right-hand pixel. The other four ($C0 $30 $0C $03) and the byte after them, $18, are not read; level 2.1's oxygen_masks are the same nine bytes.

Called by level_fire each frame of the ride. When broom_wait runs out the gauge loses a pixel: the next mask of broom_masks (step $1253, 3 down to 0) is ANDed into the eight rows of the current column; when a column is empty the next one to its left starts (broom_column, its address from broom_columns into the LDA and STA). After 24 steps, 51 + 23 x 63 = 1500 frames (30 seconds) from the start, the gauge is empty, and the next step ends the ride (broom_off). Level 2.1's oxygen_drain is the same code, which drowns Clyde instead.
The low byte of the LDA's operand at $A57E: the column being emptied (from broom_columns).
The operand of the AND at $A581: the step's mask from broom_masks.
The low byte of the STA's operand at $A583, the same column.

The broom gives out. Clyde may walk both ways again ($1272 = $FF); the special state, no-shots flag and panel flag are cleared, and so are the broom sprites' y ($1291, $1293, $D003, $D005), his jump step ($122E) and the double width ($C056); he is falling ($122A = 1) with his steps and the scroll's speed back to 1 ($2CD6, $2D35, $2D44); the four broom speeds ($1268-$126B) are zeroed; his hits left come back from saved_hits; the shot frames are blank ($0F); all three of his sprites are multicolour again ($1286 = 7) and panel sprite 1 points at 5 again. Then he drops, through the engine's fall at $2E24.
Clyde's hits left ($12A0) while he rides, kept by broom_mount and put back by broom_off.
The full gauge's eight rows, top to bottom: $55 $AA $FF $FF $AA $AA $55 $55, four two-bit pixels to the byte; level 2.1's oxygen bar uses the same rows.

Fills the gauge: broom_fill_block draws broom_bar_rows into byte columns 0-2 of panel sprite block 2 from row 13 ($40A7), then falls into broom_fill_block again for block 3 ($40E7). Level 2.1's oxygen_refill is the same code.

Draws the gauge into one sprite block: the low byte of its first byte arrives in A and goes into the STA's operand; three passes, one for each byte column, each copying broom_bar_rows' eight bytes into rows 13-20 (every third byte, X from $15 down by 3) and moving the operand on a column. Then the gauge is full: the step $1253 is 0 and broom_column 6.

Below scroll position $90 (the graveyard) it scrolls the distant graves: character $EC on three frames in four, $E0-$E3 on every other frame, $E4-$EB on one frame in four. From $90 on (the castle) it scrolls the strips of small arches by the floor: the top strip every fifth frame (rows 0-4) and every third (rows 5-7), the second every other frame (rows 1-2) and on two frames in three (rows 4-7), and the third and bottom strips on three frames in four. Each strip moves at its own pace, which gives the scenery its depth.
